python3 << 'EOF'
import re

# Let's see exactly what PARSE_RE produces for various inputs
PARSE_RE = re.compile(r"""({{|}}|{\w*(?:(?:\.\w+)|(?:\[[^\]]+\]))*(?::[^}]+)?})""")

tests = [
    '{abc',           # unclosed brace - should fail
    'test}',          # unmatched close - should fail  
    '{name}',         # valid - should work
    '{{ }}',          # escaped braces - should work
    '{name:w}',       # typed field - should work
    'text {name} more', # mixed - should work
    '{hello.world}',  # dotted name - should work
    '{data[key]}',    # dict access - should work
    '{{',             # just escaped open - valid in format string syntax
    '}}',             # just escaped close - valid in format string syntax
    'abc{def',        # unclosed brace with prefix - should fail
    'abc}def',        # unmatched close in middle - should fail
]

def validate_part(part):
    if not part:
        return True, "empty"
    if part == '{{':
        return True, "escaped open brace"
    if part == '}}':
        return True, "escaped close brace"
    # Check for problematic characters
    if '{' in part[1:] or '}' in part[:-1]:
        # Contains braces but isn't matched by PARSE_RE properly
        if part.startswith('{'):
            if part.endswith('}'):
                return True, f"field pattern: {part}"
            else:
                return False, f"starts with {{ but does not end with }}"
        else:
            if '}' in part:
                return False, "contains unmatched }"
            else:
                return False, "contains unmatched {"
    # Safe text
    return True, "regular text"

for t in tests:
    parts = PARSE_RE.split(t)
    print(f'Input: {t!r}')
    all_ok = True
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        ok, msg = validate_part(part)
        status = "OK" if ok else "ERROR"
        print(f'  PART[{i}] {status}: {msg}')
        if not ok:
            all_ok = False
    print(f'  Overall: {"OK" if all_ok else "FAIL"}')
    print()
EOF
